verdict.summary: The selective-disclosure addition is an honestly scoped, opt-in delegation seam rather than an in-repo cryptographic verifier. The acceptance path is gated by both suite support and an explicit successful host-verifier result before commitment; unsupported, unavailable, rejecting, and empty-credential paths fail closed. The public API keeps whole-credential and selective-disclosure suite token spaces separate, forwards the complete presentation to the host, attributes successful decisions to the verifier, and records only explicitly caveated provenance. Tests exercise the load-bearing fail-closed behavior, rejection behavior, token separation, verbatim forwarding, disclosed-subset commitment equivalence, provenance, and canonicalization ordering. Documentation consistently disclaims selective-disclosure soundness and unlinkability, states that external audit sq-qhy4 remains pending, updates the matching skill, and keeps the feature off by default with no new dependency.
